additional_requirements: Functioning is not markedly impaired apart from the impact of the delusion(s) or its ramifications

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

symptom.disease_info: Delusional Disorder is characterized by one or more fixed delusional beliefs lasting at least one month, with overall functioning often relatively preserved outside the area of the belief. It typically presents in mid-to-late adulthood with non-bizarre but firmly held convictions, and is distinguished from schizophrenia by the absence of prominent disorganization, negative symptoms, or broad deterioration in functioning.

patient.stressor: Peggy’s relationship with her spouse’s relatives became strained after a disagreement about money, household help, and expectations around holiday gatherings. During the following 9 months, ordinary family misunderstandings and billing discrepancies at work became connected in Peggy’s mind to a fixed belief that the in-laws were trying to undermine their reputation and financial stability, even when bank records, coworkers, and their spouse offered evidence against it. The conviction did not stop Peggy from doing routine clerical work, gardening, or painting, but it led to repeated confrontations and growing tension at home and in church circles. Peggy came to psychiatric care after their primary care clinician, hearing the same unshakable concerns across several visits, recommended a mental health evaluation.

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: I’m here because for months now I’ve been trying to get people to understand that my husband’s family is quietly messing with our money and our good name, like when little billing errors show up at work or someone at church suddenly acts funny toward me, and no matter what records anyone pulls up I know it ties back to them.

add_requirements.Functioning is not markedly impaired apa: I still get up for work, handle my billing clerk duties, keep the house going, and spend time gardening or painting; the main trouble comes up when I try to warn people about what my in-laws are doing.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: I have had more arguments with my husband and some awkward moments at church because people think I should drop it, but I have not lost my job or stopped taking care of my usual responsibilities.
add_requirements.duration: This has been going on for about nine months, ever since the trouble with my husband’s family over money and holiday expectations.
